title: Cohere: Building enterprise LLM agents that work (Shaan Desai)

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's central focus is agent architecture: single-agent vs multi-agent patterns, routing, tool specification, human-in-the-loop control, and framework selection for enterprise agent harnesses. The talk repeatedly frames its guidance around enterprise applications including customer support, HR, and financial analysis workflows. Coverage spans designing agent architectures, evaluating them with golden datasets, and deploying via Cohere's North container product. The content assumes familiarity with LLM agents and frameworks but is practical and prescriptive rather than deeply technical or research-level. This is a conference-style talk delivered by an ML engineer at Cohere. All key claims are directly stated in the transcript with supporting evidence anchors.

summary: Shaan Desai, a machine learning engineer at Cohere, presents a structured guide to building enterprise LLM agents that work in production. The talk is organized around four pillars: frameworks, approaches, evaluation, and failure mitigation, concluding with a product overview. For frameworks, he evaluates options (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangChain) against three criteria: observability, setup cost, and support. He recommends LangGraph or native builds for large-scale enterprise agents needing high observability, and AutoGen/CrewAI for quick proofs of concept due to low setup cost and multi-agent orchestration ease. For agent approaches, he strongly recommends starting simple: a single LLM with a handful of tools and meticulously specified tool definitions. He shares concrete learnings from a client engagement involving APIs with 10-15 parameters, emphasizing clear descriptions, sharp examples, simplified input types (converting nested dictionaries to list/str/float), short pithy instructions, and caching chat history beyond 20 turns to avoid hallucinations. For multi-agent setups, the router should have clear tool descriptions and sharp routing instructions covering edge cases; sub-agents should be constrained to independent tasks with small tool sets. Safety is paramount: human-in-the-loop can be codified with rules triggered before or after tool calls, exemplified by Gmail and HR support scenarios. For evaluation, Cohere builds golden datasets capturing ground truth user queries, expected function calls, parameter inputs, outputs, and final responses, enabling systematic debugging of intermediate stages. For failure mitigation, he presents a tiered strategy: prompt engineering for low-severity failures, targeted annotation datasets for 10-20% failure rates, and synthetic data generation with fine-tuning for high failure rates. Cohere continuously improves base model tool-calling performance, noting strong results on BFCL V3, a standard evaluation for single and multi-hop tool calling, with a performant 7B model for lightweight use cases. The talk concludes with an introduction to North, Cohere's single-container deployment product that packages these learnings, offering RAG, vector DB connectivity, search, and integrations with Gmail, Outlook, Drive, and Slack. A demo shows North connected to Gmail, Salesforce, and G Drive, illustrating reasoning chains, tool call transparency, and the ability to correct tool calls mid-execution.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Evaluate frameworks on observability, setup cost, and support; use LangGraph/native for enterprise scale, AutoGen/CrewAI for quick POCs.
Always start simple: a single LLM with a handful of well-specified tools can go a long way before considering multi-agent.
Tool specifications are critical: clear descriptions, sharp examples, simplified input types, and short pithy instructions dramatically improve performance.
Chat history beyond 20 turns can induce hallucinations; cache and retrieve relevant history instead of passing long context.
In multi-agent setups, the router needs clear tool descriptions and sharp routing instructions covering edge cases; sub-agents should be constrained to independent tasks.
Human-in-the-loop safety can be codified with rules triggered before or after tool calls, essential for business applications.
Build golden evaluation datasets capturing all intermediate stages (expected calls, parameters, outputs, final responses), not just final answers.
Tiered failure mitigation: prompt engineering for low severity, targeted annotation for 10-20% failures, fine-tuning with synthetic data for high failure rates.
Cohere's North product packages agentic learnings into a single container deployment with RAG, vector DBs, and app integrations (Gmail, Outlook, Drive, Slack).

sections.title: Introduction and Overview
sections.summary: Shaan Desai introduces himself as an ML engineer at Cohere and outlines the talk: introduction, frameworks, evaluation, failure mitigation, and a product overview. He notes growing demand for agents across customer support, personal assistance, RAG, and financial analysis, but highlights the difficulty of building scalable, safe, seamless agents due to the panacea of frameworks, tools, models, and evaluation criteria.

sections.title: Framework Selection
sections.summary: Discusses evaluating frameworks (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangChain) against three criteria: observability, setup cost, and support. Recommends LangGraph or native builds for large-scale enterprise agents needing high observability, and AutoGen/CrewAI for quick POCs due to low setup cost and multi-agent ease. Notes the landscape is continuously evolving.

sections.title: Agent Approaches and Tool Specification
sections.summary: Recommends starting simple with a single LLM and few tools. Shares client example with APIs taking 10-15 parameters. Key learnings: clear descriptions with sharp examples, simplified input types (nested dicts to list/str/float), short pithy instructions over long ones, and caching chat history beyond 20 turns to prevent hallucinations.

sections.title: Multi-Agent Strategies
sections.summary: Covers multi-agent orchestration (e.g., AutoGen): a router model directs to sub-agents. Router needs clear tool descriptions and sharp routing instructions covering edge cases. Sub-agents should be constrained to independent tasks with small tool sets to return final answers.

sections.title: Safety and Human-in-the-Loop
sections.summary: Emphasizes safety as paramount for scalable real-world applications. Human-in-the-loop can be codified with rules triggered before or after tool calls. Examples include Gmail agent requesting permission before sending, HR support bots, and financial analysis agents. Post-tool-call triggers useful when execution output contains sensitive information.

sections.title: Evaluation Methodology
sections.summary: Explains that successful agents need correct tool calls at the right time, accurate parameter passing, reasoning over results, and course correction. Developers care about intermediate stages, not just final output. Cohere builds golden datasets of ground truth queries, expected function calls, parameters, outputs, and final responses. Uses weather query example to illustrate intermediate stages.

sections.title: Failure Mitigation Strategies
sections.summary: Presents tiered failure mitigation: prompt engineering for low-severity/low-failure-rate issues (improving tool API specs); targeted annotation datasets for 10-20% failure rates; and synthetic data generation with fine-tuning for high failure rates involving difficult or ambiguous APIs. Transitions to bringing all components together.

sections.title: Model Improvement and North Product Overview
sections.summary: Describes Cohere's continuous improvement of base model tool-calling performance, citing strong results on BFCL V3 (a standard evaluation for single and multi-hop tool calling) with a performant 7B model for lightweight use cases. Introduces North, Cohere's single-container deployment product packaging agentic learnings with RAG, vector DB connectivity, search, and integrations with Gmail, Outlook, Drive, and Slack. A demo shows North connected to Gmail, Salesforce, and G Drive, illustrating reasoning chains, tool call transparency for debugging, SQL-like queries for conversation retrieval, and the ability to correct tool calls mid-execution. Concludes with hopes the talk provided useful learnings for deploying enterprise LLM agents.

demonstrations: Weather query example: user asks about NYC weather on Feb 5th, model should select tool, pass parameters, reason over returned results, and provide final answer like 'mostly sunny'
Client engagement with APIs taking 10-15 parameters requiring tool call optimization

North demo: connected to Gmail, Salesforce, and G Drive; model uses reasoning chains of thought to pull relevant Salesforce opportunity documents, displays reasoning chain and tool outputs for debugging; retrieves info from recent conversations using SQL-like queries; can correct tool calls mid-execution (e.g., switch from wrong tool to Gmail)
limitations: Framework recommendations are current as of the talk and expected to change as the landscape evolves
Recommendations based on past year of experience at Cohere, may not generalize to all use cases
quantitativeClaims: API specifications could take 10-15 different parameters
Chat history over 20 turns can induce hallucinations
Tool type failures or model hallucinations in the 10-20% range warrant targeted annotation datasets
Cohere's 7B model is highly performant on BFCL V3 for lightweight tool calling
